label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.13 a.8…: The name 'GOD_1' is imposed to signify something…
locator: I q.13 a.8 ad 2: ad aliquid significandum supra omnia existens, quod est principium omnium, et remotum ab omnibus
interpretation: The name 'God' is imposed to signify something existing above all, the principle of all, and remote from all; this is what those who name God intend. A nominal definition: what the name signifies, not what God is (the co.: the name is imposed from an operation, universal providence, to signify the divine nature). Kept whole, with all three conditions; not formalized. It supports, without stating, the open premise STMT-GOD-NAMES-THE-UNIQUE-MAXIME-ENS, which keeps only 'above all' (maximal in being) and 'principle of all' (cause of being of all others) and so is stronger than this reading. Per a.9 the name is communicable by its ratio, so uniqueness belongs to the thing named.
